summary: Bedřich Hrozný (1879–1952) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1897–1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1901–1902), later holding posts at Vienna (~1905–1919) and Charles University (~1919–1952).
Beihō Takashima (1875–1949) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Toyo University (~1896–1900), where he later held a post, and founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.

Bela Bhattacharya (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She served as Professor of the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011) and as Professor at the Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Ben Jiao is a Tibetology and archaeology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Case Western Reserve University in 2001 under Melvyn C. Goldstein. As of 2008, he was Deputy Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Research Institute at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Ben Joffe is a religious studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Colorado Boulder under the supervision of Carole McGranahan (attested 2019).

Benedetta Lomi specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London (~2008–2012), taught at the University of Virginia (~2015–2017), and became Senior Lecturer in East Asian Religions at the University of Bristol (~2017).

Benimadhab Barua (1888–1948) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Calcutta and a D.Litt. from the University of London (~1914–1917). He was headmaster at Mahamuni Anglo-Pali Institution (1912) and a professor at the University of Calcutta (1918–1948).

Benjamin A. Elman (born 1946) is a Sinologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania under Nathan Sivin and Susan Naquin. He taught at UCLA (1986–2002) and became Director of the East Asian Studies Program at Princeton (2002).
Benjamin Bogin is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2006) under Donald S. Lopez Jr.

Benjamin Brose specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~2004–2011) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, and served as assistant professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Michigan (~2011–2017).

Benjamin C. Ray is a religious studies scholar. He has held faculty posts at the University of Virginia, including Daniels Family NEH Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Department of Religious Studies (attested 2000, 2026).
Benjamin Goldstein works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Shayne Clarke.
Benjamin Luk Williams is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He completed his PhD at Harvard University in 2017 and held a post at Naropa University.
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1985–1989) and Harvard University (~1992–1996). He held a post at the University of Michigan around 2004.
Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Toronto under the supervision of Frances Garrett.

Benkyo Shiio (1876–1971) was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (-1915). He served as president of Taisho University (1926) and was the first director of the Sanko Cultural Institute (~1960–1971).

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya (1897–1964) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka (~1921–1925), became Director of the Oriental Institute, Baroda (1927), and founded Arya Maitreya Mandala (1933).

Benoît Vermander (born 1960) is a Sinologist and religious studies scholar educated at Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director of the Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) before joining Fudan University as professor in 2009.

Bernard Faure (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who earned a Doctorat d'État from Paris Diderot University. He held professorships at Cornell (~1983–1989), Stanford (~1990–2006), and Columbia University (~2006–2021).

Bernard Frank (1927–1996) specialized in Japanology and Buddhist studies and studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1976) and held the chair of Japanese Civilisation at the Collège de France (1979–1996).
